summary: Intermittent 429s in dedicated pool caused by healthcheck + token-refill window collision
description:
Issue summary:
ClearVoice Media reported intermittent 429 throttles impacting a critical realtime reranking route during morning traffic window on 2026-03-10. The tenant is on a Dedicated pool (eu-central) with autoscaler enabled and custom healthcheck probes configured on the ingress sidecar.

Impact:
- ~15% of requests for reranker route returned 429 over a 30-minute window (no increased error rate in downstream models).
- Customer-visible user retries and increased latency as client retries applied backoff.
- Occurred during scheduled nightly-to-day warmup handover and autoscaler eviction window.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: clearvoice-dedicated-euc-01
- Ingress: nginx-sidecar v1.12.3 behind LB (pooled IPs)
- Realtime route pinned to redwood-3-x-highthroughput (model variant)

Steps to reproduce (customer minimal repro):
1) Run sustained short-chat style requests at ~250rps for 10 minutes against their routed model (route: /v1/chat/realtime-rerank)
2) Trigger rolling healthcheck (customer uses 10s interval) and a simulated autoscaler eviction event (scale-down) during steady traffic.
3) Observe occasional 429 responses correlating with healthcheck bursts and node TTL drain.

Observed logs/snippets (sanitized):
- ingress-proxy: "healthcheck probe flood from 10.0.3.14: accepted 150 req/s"
- rate-limiter: "token_refill_epoch=2026-03-10T07:00:00Z window=60s tenant=clearvoice credits_before=120 credits_after=0"
- serving-runtime: "queue-length spike during host-eviction: 42 -> reject(429)"

Initial hypothesis:
1) Healthcheck probe fanout during node drain produced a short-lived burst which was attributed against tenant burst budget by the edge (pooled ip path), causing token exhaustion in the refill epoch.
2) Simultaneous autoscaler eviction / host TTL reset triggered a refill-window realignment between origin and edge token accounting (refill-drift), producing a sawtooth that made the tenant appear to consume credits faster than expected.
3) Because the Dedicated pool route uses strict per-tenant route weighting, background probe traffic was not isolated from interactive lanes and was counting against the same burst pool.

Customer-provided metrics attached (console screenshots referenced in comments).
investigation_notes: 03/10 07:12 UTC: Support validated customer logs and confirmed 429 spikes align with healthcheck bursts.
03/10 09:01 UTC: Infra reproduced locally by running sidecar probe flood + simulated scale-down; observed token bucket depletion in rate-limiter service during epoch boundary.
03/11 11:30 UTC: SRE measured 2s–6s refill offset between edge and origin during host eviction on dedicated pool; this matches refill-drift hypothesis.
03/11 13:20 UTC: Confirmed ingress pooled IPs can amplify probe fanout when many replicas share same nat/egress mapping (customer uses pool size 3).

Current prioritized mitigation: isolate healthcheck probe path from tenant burst pool (config change) and recommend smoothing refill window across edge/origin; evaluating rollback risk for autoscaler timing changes.
comments: Aisha Gomez (Support) 2026-03-10: Received initial customer report. Collected request IDs and console screenshots. Escalated to SRE due to dedicated pool involvement.
Liam O'Connor (SRE) 2026-03-10: Reproduced locally with probe flood harness. Attaching reproduction script and captured rate-limiter trace. Marking as in-progress.
Customer (ClearVoice) 2026-03-11: Can you confirm whether healthchecks should count against burst credits? We didn't expect internal probes to affect user traffic.

Liam O'Connor (SRE) 2026-03-11: By default probes on the same ingress path will count. We're preparing a targeted config patch to add a probe-exemption header that will exclude known healthchecks from tenant accounting on dedicated pools.

Aisha Gomez (Support) 2026-03-12: Provided customer a temporary mitigation: reduce probe concurrency to 1 and stagger probe timing across replicas. Customer acknowledged and will apply changes tonight for verification.
Engineering (Rate-Limiter) 2026-03-12: Opened INT-4120 to track core rate-limiter change to support configurable probe exemption and cross-layer refill smoothing.
workaround: Customer reduced healthcheck concurrency from 3 -> 1 and staggered probe schedule (10s offsets). Also temporarily increased route burst pool size on their Dedicated config to tolerate warmup waves. Result: 429s dropped to baseline within 45 minutes.
resolution_plan:
- Short term: release config toggle to annotate ingress probes as 'probe-exempt' for dedicated pools (hotfix).
- Medium term: schedule rate-limiter refill window smoothing in origin-edge contract to avoid epoch drift during autoscaler events.
- Long term: provide console option to separate probe/background lanes from interactive lanes for dedicated customers.
related_followups: INT-4177: autoscaler eviction timing defaults and warmup guidance
CON-987: update documentation and console UI for burst-pool/healthcheck separation
resolution: Workaround applied and validated. Hotfix for probe-exemption is targeted for 2026-03-18 pending code review. SRE will monitor dedicated pool for 72 hours post-rollout and then advise next steps.
next_steps: 1) Ship probe-exempt toggle (INT-4120). 2) Coordinate with ClearVoice to roll their probe settings back to default once hotfix is deployed. 3) Follow up to revise docs and add a dashboard tile that surfaces probe traffic vs interactive token consumption.
customer_communication: 2026-03-12: Sent status update to ClearVoice. Included mitigation steps and planned patch timeline. Customer accepted workaround and requested notification when hotfix lands.
